title: An independent look-elsewhere estimate for 616 models tested on one event
question: What effective number of independent trials do the 293 distinguishable spectra represent for a single high-energy event, does 3.4 sigma -> 2.6 sigma follow, and how does the global significance depend on the model space?
headline_result: Background-only toys over 456 WimPyDD models give N_eff = 12.2 +- 0.5 (stat) +- 1.2 (method) at local 3.4 sigma and a global 2.64 sigma, confirming LZ's 2.6 sigma; N_eff ranges 4-15 (global 2.6-3.0 sigma) with model space and grows with threshold
key_numbers: p_global(3.4 sigma)=(4.1+-0.2)e-3 (LZ 4.7e-3); N_eff=12.2 (LZ-implied 13.9); N_eff at 2.0/2.5/3.0 sigma = 4.8/6.0/8.3; heavy elastic (140 models) 4.5, inelastic grid (96) 9.9, continuous delta scan to 400 keV 9.3 (8-point grid 4.2), full+scan 14.5 (2.58 sigma); Bonferroni 293 models 1.29 sigma; robustness 8.7-13.2; background 2.92 events in 5.4-270 keV, 0.0022 above 200 keV; 300,000 toys
model_or_mechanism: profile-likelihood-ratio toy MC with toy-calibrated local p-values and min-p over model subspaces; 1D extended likelihood in observed recoil energy; WimPyDD O1,O3-O15 s/v x 13 masses + inelastic O1/O4 grid + 10 keV delta scan
stance: statistical reassessment (neutral: reproduces LZ's 2.6 sigma; 2.6-3.0 sigma depending on model space)
